title: The Angry crowd at the gate
subtitle: 江河湖海 · 主题语境阅读
theme: 江河湖海（自然生态·海洋与河流）
meta: 主题语境：江河湖海（自然生态·海洋与河流）　|　核心词汇：angry　|　正文 328 words　|　高三一轮复习
intro: 请阅读文章，根据上下文判断每一处 angry 的用法与含义，再完成 Task 1—Task 3。
passage: In 1963 the painter wrote of ① an angry crowd at the gate in the catalogue, and everybody in the studio said at once that it was ② angrier than the one named there the year before. Three seasons on, people still spoke of that morning, and of how the painter, who never explained anything, had done it without complaint and gone home; it was the angry ones, my mother said, that people remembered longest.

It was ③ the angriest crowd at the gate anybody in the studio had ever seen, or so the catalogue for May 1957 claims. My mother, who had seen them all, thought it ④ too angry to be of any use to anybody, and said as much to the visitor who had come to help; the angry ones, she used to say, were never the useful ones.

My uncle, who kept the brush at the far easel, meant something else entirely. He called the whole business ⑤ an angry sea, and said that no visitor in his right mind would call it ⑥ as angry as the sea they had once had in the old studio. He was never a man who cared whether a thing was angry or not, and he said so.

By 1970 the matter had shrunk to half a line in the catalogue. What the line asked for was ⑦ something angry, and nothing besides. The visitor from the next studio called the whole plan ⑧ quite angry; everybody laughed, and then did exactly what he had said. After that the catalogue kept the names of the angry ones only.

My mother said nothing at all. In 1973, with great care, she wrote of another angry crowd at the gate in the same catalogue, and the work, which took two seasons, seemed ⑨ angrier than anybody had expected. ⑩ The angriest sea in the whole studio, she said in 1975, was the one she could never quite name; the angry ones, she added, are always the ones that stay.

task1.title: Task 1　语境辨义
task1.intro: 请为文中十处画线形式选择对应的用法说明。
options: A. adj. 愤怒（前置定语 an angry crowd at the gate：1963 年画师在展品目录里记下的那件愤怒的人群）
B. adj. 愤怒／汹涌（比较级 angrier than：文中两处，一处比门前的人群，一处比预想）
C. adj. 愤怒／汹涌（最高级 the angriest：文中两处，见第 3、10 题）
D. adj. 愤怒（表语 too angry to do：母亲觉得它太愤怒，反倒派不上用场）
E. adj. 汹涌（前置定语 an angry sea：叔叔把整件事称作一桩汹涌的大海）
F. adj. 汹涌（同级比较 as angry as：拿眼前这桩跟旧日那桩大海相比）
G. adj. 汹涌（后置定语 something angry：修饰不定代词时须放在其后）
H. adj. 汹涌（受程度副词修饰 quite angry：那位观者的评价）

items.q: an angry crowd at the gate
the angriest crowd at the gate anybody

answers.why: angry 意为“愤怒”，1963 年画师在展品目录里记下的是“一件愤怒的人群”，此处作前置定语 an angry crowd at the gate。
angry 意为“愤怒”，此处用比较级 angrier than，拿它跟前一年记下的那一个相比。
angry 意为“愤怒”，展品目录上 五月 那行字说它是画室里最愤怒的一件，故用最高级 the angriest crowd at the gate。
angry 意为“愤怒”，母亲认为这件东西“太愤怒了，谁也用不上”，too angry to do 表示“太……以致不能”。
angry 意为“汹涌”，叔叔把整件事称作“一桩汹涌的大海”，此处作前置定语 an angry sea。
angry 意为“汹涌”，叔叔不肯说它“跟旧日那桩大海一样汹涌”，同级比较用 as angry as。
angry 意为“汹涌”，展品目录上那半行字要的是“汹涌的东西”，something 被形容词修饰时形容词须后置：something angry。
angry 意为“汹涌”，邻画室来的那位观者认为这套计划“相当汹涌”，quite 修饰原级 angry。
angry 意为“汹涌”，1973 年那趟活儿“比任何人预想的都要汹涌”，故用比较级 angrier than。
angry 意为“汹涌”，母亲 1975 年说的是“整个画室里最汹涌的那一桩”，故用最高级 the angriest sea。

task2.title: Task 2　语境运用
task2.intro: 请把下列句子译成英文，括号里是必须用到的形式。
items: 1963 年，画师在展品目录里记下了一件愤怒的人群。（an angry crowd at the gate）
人人都说它比前一年记下的那一个更愤怒。（angrier than …）
母亲觉得它太愤怒，谁也用不上。（too angry to …）
叔叔把整件事称作一桩汹涌的大海。（an angry sea）
他说，谁也不会认为它跟旧日那桩大海一样汹涌。（as angry as …）
到了 1970 年，展品目录上只剩半行字：要的是一件汹涌的东西。（something angry）
answers: In 1963 the painter wrote of an angry crowd at the gate in the catalogue.
Everybody said it was angrier than the one named there the year before.
My mother thought it too angry to be of any use to anybody.
My uncle called the whole business an angry sea.
He said nobody would call it as angry as the sea they had once had.
By 1970 the catalogue asked for nothing but something angry.

task3.title: Task 3　语境写作
task3.intro: 请写 5—6 个句子，至少使用 angry 的 3 种不同用法（前置定语、表语、比较级／最高级、后置定语等）；至少使用下列词语中的 3 个。
answers: In 1963 the painter wrote of an angry crowd at the gate in the catalogue, and nobody forgot it.
It was the angriest crowd at the gate in the studio, or so the catalogue says.
My mother thought it too angry to be of any use, and said so plainly.
My uncle called the whole business an angry sea, and nobody argued with him.
The visitor from the next studio called the plan quite angry, and everybody laughed.
The angry ones, my mother said, are always the ones that stay.
